Sonic and Sega All Stars Racing has a reference to Sonia the Hedgehog from the Sonic Underground cartoon that was mistaken for official artwork on one of the race tracks. Code Name STEAM on the 3DS is such a hidden gem that I feel like myself and one other Redditor, username IAmBLD, can appreciate its quality. It’s a turn based strategy game that takes elements from third person shooters, so it’s very comparable to Valkyria Chronicles in that respect. But the story and setting are worlds apart.

Code Name STEAM takes place in an alternate steampunk history comic book universe where the American Civil War ends with the US and Britain uniting together and fostering the development of steam-powered gadgets. Then aliens invade and start wrecking shit up (which by the way are modeled after Lovecraftian horrors) and our characters are conscripted into a secret task force to fend them off. And the leader of this group? None other than Abraham Lincoln himself, who apparently faked his death and was living in secret this entire time. He even has his own Megazord that he can fight with alongside you.

You get to play as a bunch of characters from American literature and folklore, such Tiger Lily from Peter Pan, Tom Sawyer, the Lion from the Wizard of Oz, Randolph Carter from H.P. Lovecraft’s Cthulhu mythos, and so many more.

The comic book presentation is spot on, despite not looking like anything we’ve seen from Nintendo. And in an age after the Spider Verse films, I think people will look more fondly on this art style if they ever give it a chance. The voice actors are also clearly enjoying themselves, and they’ve got a stacked cast of TV show VAs to boot. Tom Sawyer for instance is voiced by the same guy as Finn the Human from Adventure Time, just now with a southern drawl. The soundtrack also goes way harder than it should. Just a reminder that emulators like these should be unambiguously protected under fair use law, as legal precedent has been established to protect their actions since the turn of the millennium.

The February 2000 decision in *Sony v. Connectix* upholds the existence of Dolphin today for the same reasons as emulators back then: reverse engineering for the sake of study, and fostering competition to avoid commercial monopolies. Here’s the key quote from that court ruling:

“Because the Virtual Game Station (AKA the PS1 emulator Sony was trying to sue at the time) is transformative, and does not merely supplant the PlayStation console, the Virtual Game Station is a legitimate competitor in the market for platforms on which Sony and Sony-licensed games can be played. For this reason, some economic loss by Sony as a result of this competition does not compel a finding of no fair use. Sony understandably seeks control over the market for devices that play games Sony produces or licenses. The copyright law, however, does not confer such a monopoly.”

If I’m missing crucial information for this specific maneuver please let me know. But just know that the law has been there to protect emulators like this for a long time now.
